labels.label: btzcor:common_reg

hypotheses.paper: M, N E0-manifolds (Hausdorff, second countable, l.261)
hypotheses.note: E0 is the paper's own case here; the inputs (prop_cauchy_abs_max, BTZ_ext) are E0-scoped (T-btz-scope)
M, N connected added: prop_cauchy_abs_max_of_cauchyCompact_e0 is for connected M (DEC-125 (e)) and GX.BTZMax.equivalent_of_isMaximal needs Reg M connected (OQ-150 (b))
a bijective E0-morphism Reg M → Reg N (open-set structure E0LM.e0RegM); its inverse is then an E0-morphism
a homeomorphism F, E0-morphism both ways, with F ∘ val = val ∘ φ (extends the given isomorphism)

findings: BTZ_1.tex l.1278: the proof goes through the existence of BTZext(reg(M)) (Theorem theo:BTZ_ext), whose Lean form rests on the named cited input RichardsInput (Richards' theorem, l.1544–1546). Existence is not needed: M (with Reg M ↪ M) and N (with Reg M ≃ Reg N ↪ N) are already two maximal globally hyperbolic BTZ-extensions of Reg M, and the uniqueness half of theo:BTZ_ext alone (GX.BTZMax.equivalent_of_isMaximal, RichardsInput-free) identifies them. The corollary is therefore proved with no cited input.

BTZ_1.tex l.1278: « by Remark rem:reg_GH, reg(M) and reg(N) are globally hyperbolic » is not used by the Lean proof: GX.BTZMax.GHExt asks the extension, not the extended manifold, to be globally hyperbolic. It is only needed if one wants BTZext(reg(M)) to exist (the theorem's hypothesis l.1269).

BTZ_1.tex l.1278 « In particular, M and N are BTZ-maximal » is a one-line consequence of E_{≥0}-maximality (GX.BTZCommonReg.isMaximal_of_isE0Maximal) but uses that every globally hyperbolic BTZ-extension of a connected Reg M is connected (density of the image), so that the connected-target maximality of DEC-125 (e) applies.

The Lean conclusion is stronger than printed: the isomorphism M ≃ N extends the given isomorphism reg(M) ≃ reg(N) (it is the unique such extension, by density). This is what the headline btzthm:princ (l.1650–1655) needs for the injectivity of Reg.
questions: Connectedness (OQ-150 (b), OQ-142 (b)): l.261 does not require E0-manifolds connected; the corollary is proved for connected M, N. Reading taken: connected, as prop_cauchy_abs_max is in Lean (DEC-125 (e)). A componentwise form is not attempted.

« reg(M) ≃ reg(N) » (l.1275): read as an isomorphism of E0-manifolds (a bijective IsE0Mor between the open sets e0RegM, OQ-142 (a)), not as an isometry of the flat spacetimes e0RegMFlat; the two should agree but the bridge is not formalized here. In the E0 scope reg = reg_{>0}.

kb_proposals: btzcor:common_reg needs no RichardsInput: an E0-maximal M is itself a maximal GHExt of Reg M (GX.BTZCommonReg.isMaximal_regExt), and GX.BTZMax.equivalent_of_isMaximal does the rest; bridge E0AbsMax.IsE0Maximal → AbstractDev.IsMaximal is GX.BTZCommonReg.isMaximal_of_isE0Maximal.

A bijective IsE0Mor F is a homeomorphism via (Equiv.ofBijective F hb).toHomeomorphOfContinuousOpen with isOpenMap_of_isE0Mor; its inverse is IsE0Mor by GX.isE0Mor_inv_of_bijective (mathlib has no Homeomorph.homeomorphOfContinuousOpen, despite its docstring).
